newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF FRENCH OPEN FAVOURITES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF FRENCH OPEN FAVOURITES.

text.p: Profiles of the men's favourites for next week's French tennis Open:
PETE SAMPRAS (U.S.) - ATP ranking: 1. Age: 25. Height: 1.85 m. Weight: 77 kg. Grand Slam victories: US Open (4), Wimbledon (3), Australian Open (1). Best French Open result: semifinalist in 1996.

The world number one is not in his best shape ahead of the French Open. He had to pull out of the World Team Cup in Duesseldorf this week with a strained thigh. But the American, winner of the Italian Open on clay in 1994, showed last year he had the means to go all the way in Paris. Has usually done best at Roland-Garros with little preparation.
MICHAEL CHANG (U.S.) - ATP ranking: 2. Age 25. Height: 1.75 m. Weight: 68 kg. Grand Slam victory: French Open (1). Best French Open result: won 1989.

Chang has had one of his best ever seasons on hard court, winning three tournaments since the start of the year, but has struggled on clay despite winning the U.S. men's Clay Court championships in Orlando last month. Since then he crashed out early in Atlanta and Rome and seems to have lost some of the patience which made him a surprise winner here in 1989 and a losing finalist in 1995. Still one of the safest bets for victory especially as no clear favourite emerges this year.
YEVGENY KAFELNIKOV (Russia) - ATP ranking: 3. Age: 23. Height: 1.90 m. Weight: 81 kg. Grand Slam victory: French Open (1). Best French Open result: won 1996.

The player from the Black Sea looked unstoppable last year when he won both the singles and doubles titles at Roland-Garros. But this season he was sidelined for three months with a broken finger in his right hand and has struggled since. Showed some progress by reaching quarter-finals in Rome and semifinals in Hamburg. But said it "would take a miracle" for him to retain his crown.
THOMAS MUSTER (Austria) - ATP ranking: 5. Age: 29. Height: 1.80 m. Weight: 75 kg. Grand Slam victory: French Open (1) Best French Open result: won 1995.

Once the undisputed king of clay with 111 matches won on the surface in 1995 and 1996, Muster has been most unimpressive this season with only three wins on the surface. Seems to have lost his pace and power from the past and may well be paying the price for a workaholic schedule in recent years. Crashed out of the Italian Open with dehydration last week.
MARCELO RIOS (Chile) - ATP ranking: 7. Age: 21. Height: 1.75 m. Weight: 63 kg. Grand slam victories: none. Best French Open result: 4th round 1996.

The most talented player to emerge on the circuit in recent years, Rios seems to come of age this season with an impressive win in Monte Carlo and a lost final in Rome last week. He naturally masters all the shots in tennis, despite being with Chang the shortest player in the top 20 -- his serve may be his weak spot. A nightmare for interviewers, he is probably the player to watch in Paris even though he looked a bit tired in Rome and this week in St Poelten.
ALEX CORRETJA (Spain) - ATP ranking: 8. Age: 23. Height: 1.80 m. Weight: 70 kg. Grand slam victories: none. Best French Open result: 4th round 1995.

The Barcelona player has been by far the most consistent player on clay this year with wins in Estoril and Rome and a lost final in Monte Carlo. The typical clay court player, even though like compatriots Carlos Moya or Felix Mantilla he has had some fine results on hard court, Corretja leads an impressive Spanish armada. It remains to be seen whether the friendly Catalan, who speaks four languages fluently, can stand two weeks of five setters.
LEADING OUTSIDERS: Jim Courier, Sergi Bruguera, Richard Krajicek.
